study_name.evidence_quote: FMT study of metabolic syndrome patients
study_name.notes: Study name constructed from cohort description; no explicit canonical identifier provided in paper

pmid.notes: Provided as paper_id; corresponds to published Science 2016 article

target_condition.evidence_quote: FMT has shown efficacy in treating recurrent Clostridium difficile infection and is increasingly being applied to other gastrointestinal disorders
target_condition.notes: Study cohort had metabolic syndrome; FMT also discussed for R-CDI treatment

country.evidence_quote: Amsterdam UMC; Department of Vascular Medicine, Academic Medical Center, 1105 AZ Amsterdam, Netherlands
country.notes: Inferred from institutional affiliations of corresponding authors and Amsterdam location

body_site.evidence_quote: monitored strain populations in fecal samples from a recent FMT study
body_site.notes: Fecal samples explicitly stated throughout paper

days_from_first_collection.notes: Study reports time points (2 days, 42 days, 84 days post-FMT) but not individual sample collection dates relative to first collection

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: subjects in this study had not used antibiotics or other medication for at least 3 months before treatment
antibiotics_exclusion_period.notes: Explicit washout requirement stated; subjects also had no antibiotic use during treatment

antibiotics_exclusion_period_unit.evidence_quote: had not used antibiotics or other medication for at least 3 months before treatment

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Using shotgun metagenomics, we sequenced 55 fecal samples
sequencing_platform.notes: Shotgun metagenomics performed but specific platform not identified in main text or supplementary materials referenced

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: Study sequence data reported in this paper are deposited in the European Nucleotide Archive under accession number PRJEB12357
ncbi_accession.notes: ENA accession provided for all study sequence data

subject_id.notes: Paper references FMT1-5 and SELF1-5 as subject labels in figures but does not provide formal unique identifiers

sample_id.notes: Paper does not provide explicit sample identifiers; 55 fecal samples sequenced but no per-sample IDs given

control.notes: Study has FMT recipients, autologous FMT controls, and healthy controls but assignment of individual samples to case vs control role not specified

age.notes: No age data reported for study cohort; clinical parameters mentioned in table S1 but not shown in main text

age_group.notes: Age not reported; metabolic syndrome subjects typically Adult but not explicitly stated

sex.notes: Sex/gender of participants not reported in available text

family_role.notes: Not applicable; not a family-based study

location.evidence_quote: Amsterdam UMC; Academic Medical Center, 1105 AZ Amsterdam
location.notes: Inferred from primary research institution location; specific collection site not explicitly stated

westernized.notes: Westernization status not reported; study context (Netherlands, metabolic syndrome) suggests westernized but not explicitly stated

subcohort.notes: Paper describes two study groups (allogenic FMT and autologous FMT) but does not use formal subcohort identifiers

dna_extraction_kit.notes: DNA extraction method not specified in main text or accessible supplementary materials

body_site_details.notes: Fecal samples mentioned but no subsite detail provided (e.g., stool consistency, sampling method)

probing_pocket_depth.notes: Not applicable; not an oral/periodontal study

probing_pocket_depth_value.notes: Not applicable; not an oral/periodontal study

curator.notes: Curator name not provided in schema context

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: subjects in this study had not used antibiotics or other medication for at least 3 months before treatment, nor did they do so during treatment
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Applies to FMT study subjects; healthy controls' antibiotic use not reported

disease.evidence_quote: a recent FMT study of metabolic syndrome patients; 109 metagenomes of 48 healthy, FMT-naïve individuals

fmt_id.evidence_quote: FMT 1 FMT 2 FMT 3 FMT 4 FMT 5 SELF 1 SELF 2 SELF 3 SELF 4 SELF 5
fmt_id.notes: Five allogenic FMT recipients identified; SELF 1-5 are placebo controls

fmt_role.evidence_quote: half of whom received a single allogenic FMT (from one of three lean donors unrelated to the recipients) and the other half, an autologous FMT
fmt_role.notes: Study compared allogenic FMT recipients, placebo recipients, and healthy controls; three healthy donors provided FMT

treatment.evidence_quote: half of whom received a single allogenic FMT (from one of three lean donors unrelated to the recipients) and the other half, an autologous FMT (i.e., a placebo equivalent)
treatment.notes: Allogenic FMT from lean healthy donors; autologous FMT served as placebo control

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: we monitored strain populations in fecal samples from a recent FMT study on metabolic syndrome patients using single-nucleotide variants in metagenomes
biomarker_name.notes: Biomarkers used to track donor and recipient microbial strains

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: Donor-specific SNVs were most highly retained 2 days after FMT (69.3±21.8% of determinant positions)
biomarker_unit.notes: SNVs reported as percentages of determinant genomic positions

biomarker_value.evidence_quote: Donor-specific SNVs were most highly retained 2 days after FMT (69.3±21.8%) and still present 3 months later (37.6±16.6%)
biomarker_value.notes: Multiple biomarker values reported across different timepoints and conditions (allogenic FMT, placebo, healthy controls)

disease_response_os.notes: This is a microbiome study, not a clinical outcome trial; overall survival not measured

disease_response_os_unit.notes: Not applicable to this study design

ecog_performance_status.notes: Metabolic syndrome patients; ECOG status not reported

value: Dissimilarity of species composition to baseline: allogenic FMT > placebo > healthy controls
Proportion of donor-specific species: 20.1±5.0% in placebo, 17.7±10.9% in healthy individuals
Coexistence of donor and recipient strains: 50.7±10.1% of shared species
feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: extensive coexistence of donor and recipient strains, persisting 3 months after treatment
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal microbiota phenotypes characterized by microbial composition and strain coexistence patterns

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Not applicable; this is a microbiome study, not an oncology trial

value: Study population: 10 metabolic syndrome patients (5 allogenic FMT, 5 autologous/placebo)
Control group: 109 metagenomes from 48 healthy, FMT-naïve individuals
No antibiotic use for ≥3 months before or during treatment
Sampling: baseline + 4 timepoints post-treatment over 84 days
Method: shotgun metagenomic sequencing of 55 fecal samples
Primary finding: durable coexistence of donor and recipient strains for ≥3 months
Strain dominance patterns: variable across donor-recipient pairs, not associated with taxonomy or clinical outcome
Species detected: 1105 prokaryotic species; 42 species analyzed at strain level
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: cohort of 10 subjects—half of whom received a single allogenic FMT (from one of three lean donors unrelated to the recipients) and the other half, an autologous FMT
uncurated_metadata.notes: Key study design and outcome parameters not captured by standard fields

host_species.evidence_quote: fecal samples from a recent FMT study on metabolic syndrome patients
host_species.notes: Implied by study of fecal microbiota transplantation in human patients with metabolic syndrome
